draft.title: Comparing products
card: To compare products of different sizes, work out the price per unit. Price per unit = price ÷ amount.
Example: a 500 g jar of peanut butter costs $4.00 and a 750 g jar costs $5.25. $4.00 ÷ 500 = $0.008 per g, and $5.25 ÷ 750 = $0.007 per g. The 750 g jar is cheaper per gram.
Check that the units match before you divide. Change kg to g, or mL to L, so both products use the same unit.
Price is not the only thing to compare. Look at features, such as data in a phone plan, and terms, such as contract length or extra fees. The cheapest price per unit may not suit your needs.
draft.remember: Compare in the same unit, then check features and terms as well as price.

a.q: A 2 L bottle of juice costs $3.60. A 750 mL bottle costs $1.50. Which is cheaper per litre, and what is its price per litre?
opts: The 2 L bottle, at $1.80 per litre
The 750 mL bottle, at $2.00 per litre
The 2 L bottle, at $1.80 per 100 mL
The 750 mL bottle, at $1.50 per litre
a.why: $3.60 ÷ 2 = $1.80 per litre. For the small bottle, 750 mL is 0.75 L, so $1.50 ÷ 0.75 = $2.00 per litre. The 2 L bottle is cheaper per litre. Using $1.50 as the price per litre skips the unit change.
a.clue: Change 750 mL to litres before you divide.

b.q: Priya compares two phone plans. Plan X costs $40 a month and gives 20 GB of data. Plan Y costs $55 a month and gives 50 GB. Priya uses about 15 GB a month. Which statement is correct?
opts: Plan X meets her needs and costs less per month
Plan Y is better because it costs less per GB
Plan X is better because it costs less per GB
Plan Y is better because it gives more data
b.why: Plan X gives enough data for 15 GB and costs $15 less each month. Plan Y is cheaper per GB ($1.10 against $2.00), but Priya would not use the extra data. Price per unit is only useful when the extra units are needed.
b.clue: How much of the extra data would Priya actually use?

a.best: The 2 L bottle, at $1.80 per litre

b.best: Plan X meets her needs and costs less per month

problems.detail: The right option is the only one not phrased 'Plan … is better because …' and the only one that mentions her needs, echoing the stem. A student could pick it from its form alone.

'Plan Y is better because it costs less per GB' contains a true fact (Y is $1.10/GB against $2.00/GB). Asking 'Which statement is correct?' makes it unclear whether the student is judging the fact or the choice. Asking which plan suits Priya better would be clearer.
The why says 'Price per unit is only useful when the extra units are needed.' The card only says the cheapest price per unit 'may not suit your needs'. The 'only' overstates it.
